column4: 16:80 says God made animal hides into portable dwellings, light for travel and camping. The source-section’s measured, treated leather becomes a vessel; this verse gives the same material a concrete crafted use and purpose.

22:36 describes sacrificial camels whose sides fall, then directs people to eat and feed others from them. The source-section’s meysir divides a slaughtered camel by lot; this verse gives a specific, pious distribution instead, and its “sides” also meet the source-section root ج ن ب.
22:37 says the meat and blood do not reach God, but piety does. It completes 22:36’s sharing of camel meat and contrasts a game’s material prize with the intention that makes an offering acceptable.

77:20 asks whether God created people from a lowly fluid. This is another concrete creation passage corresponding to the source-section root خ ل ق and its image of shaping a thing from its starting material.
77:21 says the fluid was placed in a firm resting place. It adds the protected preparation stage after 77:20, paralleling the source-section’s making and fitting before completion.
77:22 says the fluid remains there for a known term. It makes the source-section’s dictionary sense of ق د ر as extent and endpoint concrete in a measured period of human formation.
77:23 says God determined the process and is an excellent determiner. It completes the creation, protected place, and appointed term of 77:20–22 with the source-section’s root ق د ر.

22:5 describes human formation from dust through successive womb stages, including formed and unformed, until birth and maturity. This is a specific bodily counterpart to the source-section’s stepwise craft and definition of ر ب ب as bringing a thing to completion.

40:67 traces a person from dust and a drop through birth, maturity, old age, and an appointed term. It joins the source-section’s staged formation to its claim that a thing has a measure and endpoint.
75:4 says God can proportion even the fingertips. Its root س و ي directly meets the source-section’s straightening and shaping of an arrow, here applied to the exact reconstruction of a human body.

4:10 says those who consume orphan property unjustly will burn in fire. In the same inheritance passage as assigned shares, it joins the source-section’s measured allotment to its fire verb and marks unjustly taking another’s portion as its reversal.
53:39 says a person has only what he strives for. This gives a specific alternative to the source-section’s lot-drawn meysir share: the afterlife portion follows effort rather than chance.
53:40 says the effort will be seen. It adds the accounting step between striving and repayment, clarifying how the source-section’s afterlife share is measured.
53:41 says the effort will then be repaid in full. It completes 53:39–40 with an allotted outcome based on deeds, against the source-section’s chance-assigned game share.

17:35 commands full measure and a straight balance. This is a direct practical counterpart to the source-section’s careful measurement before cutting, and makes fair measuring the boundary against manipulated shares.

6:152 commands full measure and weight in justice, then says no soul is burdened beyond its capacity. It connects the source-section’s measured making and shares to a just human measure fitted to capacity.
7:85 commands the people of Midian not to short measure or deprive people of their due. It gives a direct ethical boundary around the source-section’s making and dividing by measured portions.
11:84 places Shuayb’s warning against short measure in a community described as prosperous. It makes the source-section’s measure-and-share image a warning against turning provision into deprivation.
11:85 commands full measure and weight in justice and forbids diminishing people’s goods. It completes 11:84 with the same ethical limit relevant to the source-section’s shares.
26:181 commands full measure. In Shuayb’s speech this directly contrasts the source-section’s measured craft with the injustice of taking or giving portions by crooked means.
26:182 commands weighing with a straight balance. It specifies the just instrument in the same passage as 26:181, echoing the source-section’s straightening of a crooked thing.
26:183 forbids depriving people of their goods. It completes the measurement warning of 26:181–182 by naming the loss caused when shares are not fairly measured.
8:41 assigns fixed portions of war gains to named recipients, including orphans, the needy, and travelers. These measured shares contrast with the source-section’s chance-drawn meysir portions.
59:7 assigns communal wealth to named recipients and says it should not circulate only among the rich. It gives a specific, ordered distribution in contrast to the source-section’s game-based shares.

5:95 requires a judged equivalent animal as an offering for game killed during pilgrimage. It connects animal distribution and measured equivalence to the source-section’s game shares, and its offering term belongs to the root ه د ي that the section connects to an arrowhead.
5:96 distinguishes sea game as lawful provision from land game forbidden during pilgrimage. It completes 5:95’s hunting penalty with a clear boundary around what may be taken as food.

2:280 says an insolvent debtor should be given time until ease, using the source-section root ي س ر in a financial setting. It contrasts ease granted to someone in need with meysir as a game for dividing gains.

9:34 warns against hoarding gold and silver instead of spending in God’s way. It gives a concrete reversal to the source-section’s worldly share: accumulated wealth becomes a liability rather than an enduring portion.

9:35 describes the hoarded metal heated in Hell’s fire and used to brand foreheads, sides, and backs. It joins the source-section’s fire and measured worldly shares to its root ج ن ب for a thing’s sides, as a punishment rather than a useful vessel.
75:3 asks whether a person thinks God cannot assemble his bones. It sets up 75:4’s exact proportioning of fingertips, giving the source-section’s shaping image a resurrection counterpart.

30:54 describes the human moving from weakness to strength and back to weakness and old age. It makes the source-section’s definition of ر ب ب as bringing a thing through states concrete in the lifespan.

13:17 says rain makes valleys flow according to their capacity, while foam passes and what benefits people remains. It offers a specific image of measured capacity, fleeting excess, and retained benefit beside the source-section’s useful vessel and measured shares.
83:4 asks whether those who short measure expect to be raised. It continues 83:1–3 from fraudulent measurement to the afterlife reckoning that the source-section connects with measured shares.
83:5 identifies the resurrection as a great day. It specifies the horizon of judgment introduced in 83:4, linking unjust measure to the source-section’s lasting afterlife portion.
83:6 says people will stand before the Lord of the worlds. It completes 83:4–5’s reckoning and gives a concrete account of the source-section’s share assigned by the Lord.
